instruction: Navigate to the forms page for the Tax Division on the Department of Justice website.

metadata.explanation: This task variation asks the agent to navigate to the Tax Division forms page on justice.gov. The evaluator checks if the URL contains the pattern 'forms?title=&field_component_target_id=486' using the existing is_expected_url_pattern_match function. The task maintains the same structure and difficulty as the original Civil Division task, only changing the target division (component ID 486 instead of 431).

llm_judge_reasons: The getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts the active tab URL from Chrome's accessibility tree address bar element
The metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly performs regex pattern matching on the extracted URL
The expected pattern 'forms\?title=&field_component_target_id=486' is semantically correct and specific to the Tax Division forms page (component ID 486)
The evaluator provides complete coverage of the instruction requirement - verifying navigation to the Tax Division forms page
The verification logic will work correctly at runtime - getter extracts URL, metric checks pattern, and returns 1.0 on match
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider making the URL pattern more robust by verifying the domain (e.g., 'justice\.gov.*forms') to ensure the URL is actually on the DOJ website
The pattern could be more flexible to handle potential parameter order variations (e.g., 'field_component_target_id=486.*title=' OR 'title=.*field_component_target_id=486')
Consider whether the pattern should handle URL encoding variations (e.g., '&' vs '&')
Optional: Add anchoring to the regex pattern to ensure it matches the query string portion specifically, not just any occurrence in the URL
